findings.issue: Automatic missing-record repair can recreate an intentionally deleted record from a stale local snapshot.
findings.trigger: Another device deletes after preflight initial import/local snapshot, before the presence lookup and conditional create.
evidence: WorkingOut/Data/CloudHistoryMissingRecordRepair.swift:268 pins the local generation
WorkingOut/Data/CloudHistoryMissingRecordRepair.swift:421 treats unknownItem as missing
WorkingOut/Data/CloudHistoryMissingRecordRepair.swift:325 materializes a fresh local copy
WorkingOut/Data/CloudHistoryMissingRecordRepair.swift:339 saves it without a change tag; no server-deletion-history check distinguishes intentional deletion from failed upload
findings.scope: Separate from this user reported missing history; not proven to have occurred in their account.
findings.needed: Resolve the distinction between a failed historical upload and intentional remote deletion, and verify with a controlled cross-client test before declaring automatic repair safe.
findings.present_in_base_release_source: fc6a040 has the same pinned-inventory, unknownItem classification and nil-change-tag conditional creation logic; this risk predates the local hardening changes.

findings.issue: Deletion removes the only recoverable copy of data that never reached cloud or an external export.
evidence: 2.5 selected all-24-model history under CoachLocalOwnership.root; prepareDirectory marks root and staging directories excluded from automatic backup (CoachLocalOwnership.swift:24-35,66-70).
The retained original legacy source can be stale for later 2.5 local-only edits.
2.5.2 splits 14 legacy cloud models from 10 local-only Coach models (CloudSyncRestoration.swift:24-32).
CoachPersistence.protect excludes Coach files/photos from backup (CoachPersistence.swift:20-27).
findings.scope: A surviving external .pacebackup/export or other intact installation may help. Ordinary device/iCloud Backup cannot be assumed to include these excluded files. Cloud-only recovery cannot recreate the 10 Coach models/photos.

findings.scope: Same iCloud account, account access, surviving server records, successful normal import, and data presentation must be checked on the affected installation or a separately authorized representative Production test.

findings.issue: A profile retained in Keychain can lose its numeric units when app preferences reset on reinstall.
findings.trigger: Keychain profile survives deletion while UserDefaults unit preferences are removed.
evidence: UserProfileStore.swift:15-16 keeps unit preferences in UserDefaults; Profile at22-30 stores numeric height/target weight without unit tags.
UserProfileStore.swift:94-97 loads the Keychain values unchanged.
ContentView.swift:14-17 defaults new preferences to imperial/in/lbs.
ContentView.swift:273-279 treats a retained basic profile as onboarding-complete.
TutorialView.swift:29-53 combines retained profile numbers with newly defaulted unit preferences.
findings.example: A retained 180 cm / 80 kg profile may be interpreted as 180 in / 80 lb.
findings.scope: Keychain retention across uninstall was not tested or assumed guaranteed. This profile is outside the 24-model store test and does not explain the reported database error.

findings.issue: A portable backup can export distinct stored rows with the same UUID, then reject that backup during restore.
evidence: DataBackupService.capture maps all physical rows into UUID-based DTOs (DataBackupService.swift:306-382).
exportAll at571-586 and CoachHistoryArchive.export encode without validateForRestore.
BackupFile.validateForRestore atCoachBackupGraph.swift:862-880 rejects duplicate exercise/workout/set/run/weight/etc UUIDs.
Relationship DTOs use UUID references (DataBackupService.swift:361-362), which cannot distinguish equal-UUID physical records.
findings.scope: The restored native history deliberately preserves such distinct rows, so storage recovery success does not establish export-and-restore success. This is not evidence the affected user has duplicate IDs.
findings.needed: Provide archive identities and relationship references that can round-trip duplicate UUID rows, with a saved-file round-trip regression.

runtime_evidence.export: Actual DataBackupService.exportAll succeeded with both distinct same-UUID run rows in a 1404-byte archive.
runtime_evidence.restore_validation: Actual BackupFile.validateForRestore rejected the exported file: Duplicate run identity. No records were restored.
runtime_evidence.isolation: One full-schema generated store, separate host process, no cloud. Copied sources redirect temporary-directory getters so no unrelated export cleanup runs.

findings.issue: Preparation failures leave a gated history screen with relaunch guidance but no export or continue-local action.
evidence: ContentView.swift:70-85 offers only error and close/reopen guidance.
PersistenceController.finishDeferredStartup catches prepare failures and exposes storageError before normal views can open.
openCloudHistory local fallback only applies to container-opening failure after preparation.
findings.scope: Unknown schema, missing selected files or corrupt/tampered history should remain protected. This gap does not mean it is safe to bypass verification or that the representative historical case still fails.
findings.needed: A safe retained-file export/diagnostic recovery route and clear retain-the-installation guidance would help avoid another deletion-based workaround.
